prompt: An organization engages a worker who uses their own tools, is paid per project, and serves several other clients at the same time. Under the common-law test, this worker is most likely classified as a(n):
options: Part-Time Employee who must automatically receive employer benefits
explanation: Using their own tools, being paid by the project, and working for more than one business are contractor factors on the common-law test. Leased employees work for a staffing agency, not for themselves.

prompt: Part-time workers who resign from an organization are eligible to purchase continued health insurance coverage under:
options: PPACA, which strictly mandates employer-paid coverage for all part-time workers
explanation: Following resignation, part-time workers are eligible to purchase health insurance under COBRA rules. Part-time workers are not protected under PPACA.

prompt: Individuals who do not have an implicit or explicit contract for ongoing employment are known as:
options: Exempt Employees under the FLSA duties test
explanation: Flexible/contingent workers do not have an implicit or explicit contract for ongoing employment; core employees plan on long-term relationships.

prompt: An HR analyst reviews the status of a staff member who will not continue her employment because she is returning to school. How should the analyst classify this individual?
options: As a contingent worker, because she has no expectation of continued employment
As not a contingent worker, because she does not expect to continue for personal reasons
As a leased employee of a staffing agency
As an independent contractor under the common-law test
explanation: People who do not expect to continue for personal reasons, such as returning to school or retirement, are not contingent workers. Her short remaining tenure is a personal choice, not the absence of an ongoing-employment contract.

prompt: Two or more part-time employees performing one job is called:
explanation: Job sharing is two or more part-timers performing one job; it reduces costs, increases flexibility, maintains productivity, and may increase loyalty.

prompt: Which of the following is NOT a listed reason for the rise in use of flexible workers?
options: The shift from a manufacturing to a service economy
explanation: The slide lists recessions, international competition, and the shift from manufacturing to a service economy; new federal overtime rules are not on the list.

prompt: A compensation manager benchmarking benefits wants to compare part-time and full-time workers. Approximately what share of part-time workers have retirement benefits, compared with full-time workers?
options: About 81% of part-time workers vs. 38% of full-time workers
About 38% of part-time workers vs. 81% of full-time workers
About 50% of each, because Federal law requires equal retirement access
About 8.7% of part-time workers vs. 91% of full-time workers
explanation: Retirement benefits reach about 38% of part-time workers compared to 81% of full-time workers. The first option simply reverses the two figures.

prompt: Employers must allow part-time workers to participate in retirement plans once they meet the age and service requirements of:
explanation: Part-time workers must be allowed to participate after fulfilling the ERISA age and service requirements. COBRA concerns continued health coverage, not retirement plans.

prompt: Part-time workers are NOT protected under which of the following?
explanation: For health insurance, part-time workers are not protected under PPACA. They can still purchase COBRA coverage after resigning and must be allowed into retirement plans once ERISA requirements are met.

prompt: An organization offers its employees flextime, compressed workweeks, and telecommuting. These arrangements are collectively known as:
explanation: Flexible work schedules include flextime, compressed workweeks, and telecommuting. Contingent worker types describe who is employed, not how hours are arranged.

prompt: A company schedules its flexible employees to work during a holiday. Which policy must the company follow?
options: Pay them triple time, as Federal law strictly mandates for all holiday work
Automatically convert them to full-time status
None of the answer choices are correct
explanation: For treatment of paid time off for holidays, companies must provide alternative time off when flexible employees work during holidays.

prompt: An organization pays a worker by the hour, directly supervises the work, and provides the tools used on the job. Under the common-law test, this worker is classified as:
explanation: A worker is an employee if the employer controls/supervises, provides tools and location, and pays by the hour or time worked.

prompt: Which of the following factors appears in the economic realities test?
explanation: Economic realities factors are integration, investment in facilities, right to control, risk (profit or loss), skill, and continuing relationship. Intent, method of payment, and type of business are common-law factors.

prompt: An HR analyst finds that a worker has made a substantial investment in the work facilities and equipment. Under the economic realities test, this factor points toward:
explanation: On the economic realities test, a substantial investment in facilities and equipment points toward contractor status.

prompt: Which of the following individuals is NOT a contingent worker?
options: An employee who plans to leave in May to return to graduate school
A seasonal warehouse worker hired through December 31
A consultant engaged for a six-month project
explanation: Leaving for personal reasons (e.g., school, retirement) does not make someone contingent; the professor repeated this in the video. Part-timers, seasonal hires, and project consultants lack a contract for ongoing employment.

prompt: A leased employee is legally the employee of:
options: The client organization where the work is performed
Neither, because leased employees are always legally self-employed
Both, jointly and equally under federal law
explanation: A leased employee belongs to the staffing agency: the client pays the agency, and the agency pays the worker.

prompt: An HR director preparing a workforce plan summarizes the three reasons given for the rise in use of flexible workers. Which of the following is NOT one of those reasons?
options: The passage of the Family and Medical Leave Act
The shift from manufacturing to a service economy
explanation: The three reasons are recessions, international competition, and the manufacturing-to-service shift; the FMLA is not one of them.

prompt: Regarding benefits for part-time workers, which of the following statements is accurate?
options: Federal law requires employers to offer them health insurance under PPACA
They are legally ineligible for COBRA coverage after resignation
Retirement is a legally required benefit for all workers
Employers must allow them into retirement plans once ERISA age and service requirements are met
explanation: Employers must allow retirement participation once ERISA thresholds are met. Part-timers are not protected under PPACA, can buy COBRA coverage, and retirement is a discretionary benefit.

prompt: “Investment in facilities” and “risk of profit or loss” are factors found in:
explanation: These are economic realities test factors only; neither appears on the common-law list.

prompt: An organization adopts a compressed workweek for its staff. Which form does a compressed workweek most commonly take?
explanation: Four 10-hour days is the most common form. Three 12-hour days (36 hours) also appears, but 4×10 is most common.

prompt: Which of the following statements about part-time employees is accurate?
options: They are always considered core employees
They are legally classified as independent contractors
None of the answer choices are correct
explanation: Part-time employees are considered contingent workers. Core employees are those who plan on a long-term relationship.

prompt: A private organization’s HR manager is reviewing its holiday policy. Which statement about federal holidays is accurate?
options: Federal law requires all private organizations to close on federal holidays
Private organizations are not legally required to close on federal holidays
Private organizations must close on federal holidays only if they employ flexible workers
None of the answer choices are correct
explanation: Private organizations are not legally required to close on federal holidays. That is exactly why the rule to provide alternative paid time off exists.

prompt: A retailer hires three workers for the holidays with a definite stop date. The stop date is what makes these workers:
explanation: A definite stop date means there is no contract for ongoing employment, so the workers are contingent.

prompt: Two part-time employees split one full-time job. Which of the following is NOT one of the four listed effects of job sharing?
options: Guarantees benefits eligibility under federal law
explanation: The four effects are: reduces costs, increases flexibility, maintains productivity, and may increase loyalty. Job sharers typically are not benefit-eligible.

prompt: “Intent” and “method of payment” are factors on which test?
explanation: Intent, tools, supervision, method of payment, type of business, and working for more than one firm are common-law factors only.

prompt: An employee drops her child off at 8:15, starts work at 8:30, leaves at 3:15, and finishes her hours remotely. This arrangement is called:
explanation: Working different times of the day is flextime. A compressed workweek fits full-time hours into fewer days, which is not happening here.
